findings.message: Detected user input used to manually construct a SQL string. This is usually bad practice because manual construction could accidentally result in a SQL injection. An attacker could use a SQL injection to steal or modify contents of the database. Instead, use a parameterized query which is available by default in most database engines. Alternatively, consider using the Django object-relational mappers (ORM) instead of raw SQL queries.

findings.message: Found user input going directly into typecast for bool(), float(), or complex(). This allows an attacker to inject Python's not-a-number (NaN) into the typecast. This results in undefind behavior, particularly when doing comparisons. Either cast to a different type, or add a guard checking for all capitalizations of the string 'nan'.
cwe: CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast
findings.triage_reason: float(request.form['score']) is followed immediately by math.isfinite() and a 0..max_score range check, so 'nan', 'inf' and out-of-range values raise ValueError and are rejected with an error message (tested: score 999 is refused).
findings.remediation: Keep the isfinite() guard on every float() of user input. Optional: validate the raw text with a strict regex such as ^\d{1,4}(\.\d{1,2})?$ before converting.

findings.message: Be careful with `flask.make_response()`. If this response is rendered onto a webpage, this could create a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. `flask.make_response()` will not autoescape HTML. If you are rendering HTML, write your HTML in a template file and use `flask.render_template()` which will take care of escaping. If you are returning data from an API, consider using `flask.jsonify()`.
cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
findings.triage_reason: The response body is the CAPTCHA SVG generated on the server from a fixed character set - no user input reaches it. It is served as image/svg+xml with Content-Security-Policy default-src 'none' and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, so it cannot run script.
findings.remediation: No change needed. Keep the explicit mimetype and the CSP header.

findings.message: Detected explicitly unescaped content using 'Markup()'. This permits the unescaped data to include unescaped HTML which could result in cross-site scripting. Ensure this data is not externally controlled, or consider rewriting to not use 'Markup()'.
cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
findings.triage_reason: Markup() marks the QR-code SVG made by the qrcode library as safe HTML. Its input (the username and a random base32 secret) is encoded as QR square geometry, never as text or tags, and the page CSP blocks all scripts.
findings.remediation: Optional hardening: serve the QR code from a separate /mfa/qr.svg route and show it with an tag, so Markup() is no longer needed.

findings.message: Manually-created forms in django templates should specify a csrf_token to prevent CSRF attacks.
findings.triage_reason: This is a Django rule that looks for {% csrf_token %}. UniPortal is a Flask app: every POST form contains {{ csrf_field() }} and security.csrf_protect() rejects any POST without a valid token (DAST check 'Login POST without CSRF token rejected' returns HTTP 400).
findings.remediation: No change. For future scans exclude Django-only rules (e.g. --exclude-rule python.django.security.django-no-csrf-token.django-no-csrf-token).
